invariants: Safety gate is absolute in every mode: the PROD_PROJECT_REFS denylist beats every flag and no password ever surfaces. Two target modes (extracted + hardened from wedge-repro.ts): assertStagingTarget (positive allowlist — ref must EQUAL KNOWN_STAGING_REF; used by wedge-repro + burst-drill-load on shared staging) and assertEphemeralBranchTarget (ref must equal --confirm-branch AND be neither prod nor KNOWN_STAGING_REF; used by the differential on a throwaway branch)

db_touching=false means no schema/migration and no new production tenant-scoped query site (so the tenant-scope/RLS audits are unaffected); the staging scripts DO perform operational INSERT/DELETE against job_outbox at runtime, guarded by the safety gate + scoped-delete predicate + their tests

No production runtime BEHAVIOR change — the health bundle stays sequential (ADR 0008); the differential reproduces the wedge with its OWN concurrent client, never by reverting runHealthChecks. The ONLY production edit is adding `export` to the existing pure resolveHealthAlertConfig in checks.ts (visibility only, zero behavior change, no new production caller — approved surface amendment for the single-owner fix)

Single owner of the health-bundle query mix AND its config — the differential reuses the exported checkXxx functions and the exported resolveHealthAlertConfig, never re-copies their SQL or config resolution (so both concurrent and sequential arms fire byte-identical query parameters)
Single owner of backlog-depth counting — the drill reads backlog via queryBacklogDepth / GET /internal/queue-health, never a re-implemented count
Never log raw review/response text, tokens, or secrets — the scripts observe pids/counts only
No new runtime dependency; no package.json / pnpm-lock change

The differential runs against an EPHEMERAL Supabase branch where it is the sole client (ADR-0007 app_name flattening makes pooler attribution impossible; the branch dissolves it). Cleanup on every exit path incl. SIGINT/SIGTERM: client.end + pg_terminate_backend of ALL wedge-signature backends on the isolated branch (safe — nothing else is there) + a zero baseline barrier between arms; final teardown = operator delete_branch. The prod denylist still guards terminate-all as defense-in-depth (resource-ownership contract, D5)
edge_cases: Differential baseline arm does NOT wedge on a given iteration → reported honestly as a non-repro finding, not masked (wedge-repro precedent)
Injected drill rows must dispatch cleanly (mocked/benign) so the drill produces no spurious outbox_failed / stale_dispatching health alerts beyond the intended backlog_depth
Over-threshold arm must drain back under 1500 so backlog_depth CLEARS — otherwise the alert stays latched and pollutes later drills
The drill must not run concurrently with wedge-repro.ts or the differential (both perturb the pooler / backlog observation)
Drain is dispatch-bound (OutboxPoller ~600/min), not LLM-completion-bound — the 30-min target is on job_outbox pending count; documented so the number isn't misread
SIGINT/SIGTERM mid-run must still kill children + terminate attributed backends before exit
